## Summary

Second vertical slice of the v0.1 CLI. Combined with [#4 (`pack`)](https://github.com/mc856/codex/pull/4), the protocol's core loop is now usable end-to-end:

```bash
contextspec init
contextspec create initiative q2-onboarding-pulse --domain onboarding --project web-app
contextspec pack --role engineer --initiative q2-onboarding-pulse --task review
```

Both spec-form (`create initiative <id>`) and convenience form (`create-initiative <id>`) are accepted. The two-word form is collapsed to the single-token form before cac sees it, since cac treats command names as single tokens.

## What `init` writes

A minimal but realistic skeleton:

- `registry.yaml` (v0.1, three roles + commented stubs for `sources` / `domains` / `projects`)
- `context.md`, `principles.md`, `glossary.md`, `constraints.md`
- `roles/{pm,growth,engineer}.md` — distilled, generic role contracts (mission, owns, needs, output contract, cannot-decide, checklist, common mistakes, suggested memory updates)
- `memory/{README,anti-patterns,experiment-results}.md`

Refuses to overwrite existing files unless `--force`.

## What `create-initiative` writes

`initiatives/<id>/` with the six template files in §5.7 load order: `brief.md`, `context-map.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `acceptance.md`, `decisions.md`. `retro.md` and `reviews/` are post-completion only and are not pre-created. An empty `packs/` directory is created so users can find the pack output destination.

The initiative is registered in `registry.yaml` **in place**, by manipulating the YAML AST so:

- comments are preserved
- existing initiatives stay where they are
- the `initiatives:` mapping is converted from flow-style (`{}`) to block style so subsequent diffs stay clean

Unknown roles / domains / projects produce warnings rather than errors — users can register initiatives before fully populating the registry, since `pack` will warn about missing references later.

## Tests

`npm test` — 28 cases, 12 new in `test/init.test.ts`:

- `init` writes the right files; produces a registry that `loadRegistry` validates; refuses without `--force`; `--force` overwrites
- `create-initiative` writes templates; registers in registry; default roles = all declared roles; validates kebab-case ids; rejects duplicates; `--force` re-registers; warns on undeclared domain/project; errors when registry.yaml is absent
- preserves comments and second-initiative entries on subsequent runs
- end-to-end: a fresh `init` + `create-initiative <id>` produces a project that compiles cleanly via `compilePack` with no warnings or skipped files

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm install && npm run build && npm test` passes locally
- [ ] In a scratch dir: `node bin/contextspec.js init && node bin/contextspec.js create initiative demo && node bin/contextspec.js pack --role engineer --initiative demo --task review` produces a non-empty pack
- [ ] Skim a generated `registry.yaml` after two `create-initiative` runs and confirm comments + ordering survive

## Out of scope (deferred)

- `contextspec generate claude` / `generate codex` (next slice)
- npm publish / CI
- `contextspec validate` / `--check` mode

body:
## Description
This PR fixes an issue where Presto fails to insert data into Iceberg tables created by Apache Flink, Spark, etc. The failure occurs because other engines create tables using the deprecated Iceberg property `write.object-storage.path`, but the Apache Iceberg library (version 1.9.0+) throws an IllegalArgumentException when encountering this deprecated property [here](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/apache-iceberg-1.9.0/core/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/LocationProviders.java#L87).

The fix implements property sanitization that automatically converts deprecated Iceberg properties to their modern equivalents before passing them to the Iceberg library, ensuring backward compatibility with tables created by other systems like Flink, Spark, etc.

**Error before fix:**

```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Property 'write.object-storage.path' has been deprecated 
and will be removed in 2.0, use 'write.data.path' instead.
```

## Motivation and Context
Other engines may add the deprecated write.object-storage.path property when creating Iceberg tables. Apache Iceberg library (1.9.0+) rejects this deprecated property with an exception, and currently Presto is using an upgraded version of Iceberg, which would throw an error for deprecated Iceberg properties listed [here](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/apache-iceberg-1.9.0/core/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/LocationProviders.java#L80).

## Impact
Presto can now successfully read and write to Iceberg tables created by other engines and maintains backward compatibility.

## Summary by Sourcery

Sanitize deprecated Iceberg table properties to maintain compatibility with newer Iceberg versions and external engines using legacy settings.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent write failures when handling tables that use the deprecated write.object-storage.path property by converting it to the supported write.data.path property before invoking Iceberg APIs.

author: arturovt
body:
Introduces a new `warnOnNewReferenceWithIdenticalValue` option to `NgxsDevelopmentOptions`. When configured, `selectSignal` will warn in dev mode if a selector returns a new reference whose value is considered equal by the provided `isEqual` function, indicating unnecessary signal recomputation.

The option requires a user-supplied `isEqual` implementation (e.g. lodash `isEqual`) rather than relying on `JSON.stringify`, which is prohibitively slow inside a signal equality check.

Closes #136

## What's in

\`RunTimeline\` — multi-lane execution timeline showing run phases over time, the final primitive for issue #136:

- Each phase renders as a colored bar positioned by its \`start\` / \`end\` and routed to a lane by \`laneId\`.
- Optional \`cursor\` draws a thin vertical line for the current playback position. Pair with \`TimelineScrubber\` to drive it.
- States: \`queued\` (amber) / \`running\` (blue) / \`complete\` (emerald) / \`failed\` (red) / \`stopped\` (muted).
- Single-lane mode (drop \`lanes\`) falls back to a default \`"Run"\` lane.
- Phases whose \`laneId\` doesn't match any provided lane are skipped without warning.
- When \`end\` is not greater than \`start\`, the timeline falls back to a 1-unit span.
- Optional \`onActivate\` per phase makes the bar a button (otherwise a plain span).

Pure presentation; the host computes the phase list from the run's execution history. Wired into the \`@vllnt/ui\` barrel and the shadcn registry.

Distinct from \`MapTimeline\` (geo-aware), \`Stepper\` (sequential steps), and the timeline family issues \`#32\`–\`#35\`: this primitive is specifically the run history surface inside the canvas.

D3.1 of [MIGRATION_PLAN_RASTER_COMPLETION.md § D3](MIGRATION_PLAN_RASTER_COMPLETION.md) — introduces the `org.skia.codec` package with the `SkCodec` decoder facade and the first concrete codec, PNG, via `javax.imageio`.

Two decode paths : 16-bpc raster → premul F16 (raw raster read, skips ImageIO's `getRGB` quantisation), 8-bpc → 8888 via `getRGB` (documented to return non-premul ARGB regardless of the underlying buffer type — fixes a 1-2 ulp drift the legacy Graphics2D-based path had on translucent pixels).

body:
## Summary
Path B doc-only RCA for issue #529 (notification re-inject loop on rate-limit recovery, observed during dev's Sprint 55 P0-B FINAL smoke on 2026-05-08). Distinguishes the (a) daemon-side hypothesis from (b) backend scrollback retrigger using direct event-log evidence + code-path audit.

**Verdict:** (a)-class only. Track G can land Option A (per lead's conditional dispatch).

## Root cause (one-liner)
`src/daemon/supervisor.rs::process_server_rate_limit_retries` re-injects `last_input_text` up to 3 times on the `[5, 15, 30]`s backoff after an agent enters `AgentState::ServerRateLimit`. When the most-recent input was a `[AGEND-MSG]` notification, the same notification body is what gets replayed. The retry mechanism is content-blind, so inbox-class deliveries (whose body is durably persisted in `~/.agend/inbox/`) are inappropriately re-played alongside legitimate keystroke retries.

## Direct event-log evidence (cheerc-class repro window)
`grep "2026-05-08T07:4" ~/.agend-terminal/event-log.jsonl | grep server_rate_limit`:

```
2026-05-08T07:42:37 — server_rate_limit_retry      instance=dev   attempt 1
2026-05-08T07:42:57 — server_rate_limit_retry      instance=dev   attempt 2   (Δ +20s)
2026-05-08T07:43:27 — server_rate_limit_retry      instance=dev   attempt 3   (Δ +30s)
2026-05-08T07:43:57 — server_rate_limit_exhausted  instance=dev   gave up after 3 retries  (Δ +30s)
```

Deltas match `SERVER_RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF = [5, 15, 30]` to the second. Pattern is structurally inconsistent with random scrollback retrigger or stuck pickup tracking.

## Why other dimensions don't explain the symptom
| Dimension | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| §1 (a) daemon-side re-inject loop | **ROOT CAUSE** | `process_server_rate_limit_retries` lines 442-543 + 4 retry events match symptom timestamps |
| §2 (b) scrollback retrigger | OUT | Timing matches daemon backoff exactly, not random; no non-daemon inject events at symptom times |
| Pickup-tracking (`pending_pickup_ids`) | OUT | Channel-side reaction tracker; not read by retry mechanism |
| Poll-reminder | OUT | Already has count-keyed dedup via `LAST_NOTIFIED` |

## Fix shape recommendation for Track G (Path A, ~30-50 LOC)
1. Add `last_inject_id` (notification fingerprint) to `RateLimitRetry`.
2. Before phase-2's `inject_to_agent`, dedup against the fingerprint within an in-window threshold (e.g. 60s) — skip when same fingerprint mid-stall.
3. Force-inject when fingerprint differs (keystroke retry stays intact) or heartbeat-after-rate-limit recovery is observed.
4. Per-fingerprint cap of ~1-2 alongside existing global `MAX_RETRIES=3`, with `notification_inject_dedup_capped` event for audit.

The simpler "skip retry entirely if `last_input_text` starts with `[AGEND-MSG]`" rule is documented as rejected — it would lose legitimate keystroke retry coverage.

## Operator escape hatch (zero-LOC, available today)
Drain inbox quickly when the agent recovers — the `inbox` MCP tool clears the pending notification. If the loop is consistently noisy, lower `SERVER_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RETRIES` from 3 to 1 (fragile; loses keystroke retry coverage). Track G is the durable fix.

- [x] Direct event-log correlation pulled from `~/.agend-terminal/event-log.jsonl` for the 2026-05-08T07:42-07:43 window (4 events for instance=dev, perfect backoff match)
- [x] Production sites of `last_input_text =` audited (3 sites: inbox.rs, layout/pane.rs, api/handlers/instance.rs) — all populate `text` (raw body) which is what gets replayed

## Summary

Fixes the two residual findings from the 2026-05-08 OWASP audit (`audit/2026-05-08/security-report.md`). Risk score 8 → 0.

- **A02 Medium — `WEBHOOK_INVESTEC_SECRET` never reached the container.** `.env.template` documented the variable but `docker-compose.yml` didn't propagate it, so operators following the documented setup silently deployed with the realtime card-push webhook permanently failing closed (every `POST /api/webhook/investec` returns 401). Wired the env var through using the .NET config provider's double-underscore mapping (`Webhooks__InvestecSecret`) so it binds to `_configuration["Webhooks:InvestecSecret"]` that `WebhookController.ValidateSecret` already reads. The `:-` default preserves the fail-closed posture when the operator hasn't configured the secret yet.

- **A03 Medium — Tailwind play CDN was unversioned and unhashable.** All three SPA entry points loaded `https://cdn.tailwindcss.com` (latest, no SRI), so a CDN compromise yielded full DOM control on the authenticated dashboard. The play CDN ships a JIT compiler rather than a fixed bundle, so a stable SRI hash isn't published — the strongest assertion the CDN supports is the versioned URL. Pinned `index.html`, `pricing.html`, and `side-hustle.html` to `cdn.tailwindcss.com/3.4.17` and added `crossorigin="anonymous"` / `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` for defence in depth. body:
# PR Description

## Summary

Fixes a 5/5-reproducible installation failure in cert-manager-operator v1.16.0 where
the operator pod immediately produces `RoleBindingCreateFailed` and `RoleCreateFailed`
errors and remains in a `Degraded` state indefinitely.

## Root Cause

Two bugs compound to prevent clean installation:

**1. Role/RoleBinding applied in wrong order**

All three static resource controllers list RoleBindings before their referenced Roles
in their asset file slices. `ApplyDirectly` processes files sequentially, so RoleBindings
hit the Kubernetes RBAC admission controller before the Roles they reference exist.
This affects 4 pairs across 3 files.

**2. Operator ClusterRole missing `serviceaccounts/token`**

The new `cert-manager-tokenrequest` Role (v1.16.0) grants `serviceaccounts/token create`
to the `cert-manager` ServiceAccount. Kubernetes RBAC escalation prevention requires the
creating principal to already hold this permission — but the operator's ClusterRole only
listed `serviceaccounts`, not `serviceaccounts/token`. This makes the tokenrequest failure
**permanent** (unlike the leaderelection/dynamic-serving pairs, which would self-heal once
their Roles are eventually created).

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `pkg/controller/deployment/cert_manager_controller_deployment.go` | Moved `cert-manager-leaderelection-role.yaml` and `cert-manager-tokenrequest-role.yaml` before their respective RoleBindings |
| `pkg/controller/deployment/cert_manager_cainjector_deployment.go` | Moved `cert-manager-cainjector-leaderelection-role.yaml` before its RoleBinding |
| `pkg/controller/deployment/cert_manager_webhook_deployment.go` | Moved `cert-manager-webhook-dynamic-serving-role.yaml` before its RoleBinding |
| `config/rbac/role.yaml` | Added `serviceaccounts/token` to `""` apiGroup resources |
| `bundle/manifests/cert-manager-operator.clusterserviceversion.yaml` | Synced `serviceaccounts/token` into `clusterPermissions` |
| `pkg/controller/deployment/asset_ordering_test.go` | New regression tests (3 assertions) |

**Net change:** +6 insertions, −4 deletions in production code; +105 lines of tests.

## Tests

Three regression tests added in `pkg/controller/deployment/asset_ordering_test.go`:

- `TestRoleBeforeRoleBinding` — verifies Role precedes RoleBinding in all three asset slices
- `TestOperatorClusterRoleHasServiceAccountsToken` — verifies `config/rbac/role.yaml` has the sub-resource
- `TestBundleCSVHasServiceAccountsToken` — verifies bundle CSV is in sync

All three tests were confirmed to **FAIL on the original broken code** and **PASS on this fix**.

Full test suite: `go test ./...` — all packages with tests pass (`api/operator/v1alpha1`,
`pkg/controller/deployment`, `pkg/controller/istiocsr`, `pkg/features`). One pre-existing
build failure in `hack/typelinter` (vendored `golang.org/x/tools` incompatibility) is
unrelated to this change.

## Known Limitation / Follow-up

The `serviceaccounts/token` sub-resource was added to the existing broad `""` apiGroup rule,
inheriting all verbs (create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch). Only `create` is
required for RBAC escalation prevention and is the only verb cert-manager uses. The extra
verbs are effectively no-ops on the Kubernetes TokenRequest API endpoint, but a follow-up
PR could narrow this to a minimal `create`-only rule for cleaner least-privilege hygiene.

## Reproduction

```
# Original error in operator pod logs (v1.16.0):
I0527 18:07:38.460719 1 event.go:377] type: 'Warning' reason: 'RoleBindingCreateFailed'
  Failed to create RoleBinding...cert-manager-cert-manager-tokenrequest: 
  roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "cert-manager-tokenrequest" not found

I0527 18:07:38.885813 1 event.go:377] type: 'Warning' reason: 'RoleCreateFailed'
  roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "cert-manager-tokenrequest" is forbidden:
  user "system:serviceaccount:cert-manager-operator:cert-manager-operator-controller-manager"
  is attempting to grant RBAC permissions not currently held:
  {APIGroups:[""], Resources:["serviceaccounts/token"], ResourceNames:["cert-manager"], Verbs:["create"]}
```

- [x] Regression tests added and verified against original broken code
- [x] `go build ./...` passes
- [x] `go vet ./pkg/controller/deployment/...` passes
- [x] `gofmt` clean
- [x] `config/rbac/role.yaml` and bundle CSV kept in sync

body:
## Summary
Two waves of fixes for issues surfaced live during a Claude Desktop MCP demo against a mixed `drop/` folder of PPTX + XLSX.

### Wave 1 — folder-mode discovery filters to tabular files
- `discover_corpus_schema` and `ingest_corpus_structured` (folder mode) now skip non-tabular files (PPTX, PDF, DOCX, …). Mixed drop folders no longer crash schema discovery with `UnicodeDecodeError` from a PPTX byte being read as a CSV.
- `_sample_for` raises a clear `ValueError` for unsupported suffixes; `_csv_sample` opens with explicit UTF-8 and translates a real Latin-1 / CP1252 encoding error into a useful hint.

### Wave 2 — parallel-safe MCP corpus access
Specs: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-08-mcp-corpus-concurrency-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-08-mcp-corpus-concurrency.md`.

- **Process-wide `_AGENT_CACHE`** in `corpus_rag.py` — every tool call against a `corpus_id` now shares one `CorpusAgent` / `DatabaseStore` / `LocalBackend` (and one real `asyncio.Lock`).
- **Per-corpus `_WRITE_LOCKS`** at the tool layer — write tools serialise on it; reads stay lock-free.
- **`ingest_structured` goes through `db_store.for_write()`** — no more raw `sqlite3.connect(db_path)` bypassing the storage lock. Fixes "database disk image is malformed" under parallel writes.
- **`_sync_ingest_table` tightened**: `timeout=30`, `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000`, autocommit + explicit `BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK`, `log.warning` on rollback failure (no silent errors).
- **`LocalFolderSourceConfig.exclude_predicate`** — `ingest_corpus_filesystem` skips CSV / XLS / XLSX (handled by `ingest_corpus_structured`), so spreadsheets aren't double-represented.
- **FastMCP lifespan hook** — `create_mcp_app(*, lifespan=...)` plumbed through; `examples/corpus_search/mcp_server.py` now closes cached agents on shutdown.
- **WAL checkpoint before upload** — `DatabaseStore.for_write` runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` on the cache file before handing it to the backend's `shutil.copyfile`. Without this, writes left in `<cache>-wal` by long-lived `SqliteCorpus` connections were silently dropped from the uploaded artifact. **Surfaced by the new integration test.**

## Why
- Demo session #1 (mixed drop folder): `discover_corpus_schema` exploded with `UnicodeDecodeError: 0xBA …` from a PPTX byte read as CSV.
- Demo session #2 (parallel ingest): `database disk image is malformed`, 25k partial rows, 0 unstructured chunks.

| | Before | After |

## Summary

author: zuyeyang
body:
## Problem

`extract_sql()` misses foreign key relationships defined via `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES` — it only extracts inline `REFERENCES` within `CREATE TABLE` column definitions.

Many real-world schemas (pg_dump output, enterprise databases) define FK constraints separately. For example, [AdventureWorks](https://github.com/lorint/AdventureWorks-for-Postgres) (68 tables, 5 schemas) defines all 89 FK relationships via ALTER TABLE — graphify currently finds **zero** of them.

Additionally, `_obj_name()` only reads the first `identifier` child of `object_reference` nodes, so schema-qualified names like `Sales.Customer` are truncated to just `Sales`.

## Goal

Make graphify's SQL parser reliable enough that downstream tools can consume `graph.json` as the single source of truth for database schema relationships — instead of re-parsing SQL with regex.

## Changes

**`graphify/extract.py`:**
- **`_obj_name()`**: Read the full `object_reference` text instead of just the first `identifier` child. This preserves schema-qualified names (`Sales.Customer`) while keeping bare names (`users`) unchanged.
- **`walk()` — new `alter_table` handler**: Extract FK edges from `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES`. Reuses existing `table_nids` lookup to connect to previously-seen CREATE TABLE nodes.
- **Inline FK + `_walk_from_refs()`**: Same fix — read full `object_reference` text for schema-qualified references.

**Tests:**
- `test_sql_alter_table_fk_edge` — ALTER TABLE FK produces a `references` edge with no dangling nodes
- `test_sql_schema_qualified_names` — `Sales.Customer` label is preserved (not truncated to `Sales`)
- `test_sql_schema_qualified_alter_fk` — ALTER TABLE with schema-qualified names produces correct edges

All 6 existing SQL tests continue to pass.

## Before / After

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| AdventureWorks FK edges | 0 | 89 |
| Schema-qualified name `Sales.Customer` | Parsed as `Sales` | Parsed as `Sales.Customer` |

## Downstream use case

I uses graphify's `graph.json` to auto-generate per-table schema documentation for AI database agents. Without ALTER TABLE FK extraction, it had to re-implement SQL parsing with regex — this PR eliminates that need.

## Summary

Cookies name more stuff than just processes. The kernel has builtin socket cookies and Pedro will eventually assign cookies to inodes and possibly cgroups. The 64-bit cookie structure can spare 2-3 bits to identify the cookie type easily:

- Process cookies start with a 42-bit timestamp at ~4ms granularity, which can easily drop 2 MSBs and still be good for hundreds of years
- Inode and cgroup cookies are going to be similar
- Socket cookies similarly begin with a timestamp

Storing 2 bits of the cookie type is beneficial, because it allows logs to unambiguously identify an object without having to separately store its type. This is especially handy if you're logging generic "target:instigator" pairs where the target could interchangeably be a process or e.g. a socket.

Also includes a minor fix to clp2().
